   101	/-- The Yoneda functor from group objects to group-valued functors is fully faithful. -/
   102	def pointsYoneda : Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat :=
   103	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrp
   104	
   105	def pointsYoneda_fullyFaithful : (pointsYoneda (C := C)).FullyFaithful :=
   106	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpFullyFaithful

   108	/-- Composition with a right translation is multiplication in the Hom-group. -/
   109	theorem comp_mulRight_hom (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   110	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).hom = f * (toUnit X ≫ g) := by
   111	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_hom, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   112	    comp_toUnit_assoc, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
   113	
   114	/-- Composition with the inverse right translation is multiplication by the inverse. -/
   115	theorem comp_mulRight_inv (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   116	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).inv = f * (toUnit X ≫ g)⁻¹ := by
   117	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_inv, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   118	    ← Category.assoc, comp_toUnit, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def,
   119	    CategoryTheory.Hom.inv_def, Category.assoc]
   120	
   121	/-- The translation carrying the section `x` to the section `y`. -/
   122	def pointTranslation (G : C) [GrpObj G] (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) : G ≅ G :=
   123	  (GrpObj.mulRight x).symm ≪≫ GrpObj.mulRight y
   124	
   125	@[simp]
   126	theorem pointTranslation_self (x : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   127	    pointTranslation G x x = Iso.refl G := by
   128	  simp [pointTranslation]
   129	
   130	@[simp]
   131	theorem pointTranslation_symm (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   132	    (pointTranslation G x y).symm = pointTranslation G y x := by
   133	  simp [pointTranslation]
   134	
   135	@[simp]
   136	theorem pointTranslation_trans (x y z : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   137	    pointTranslation G x y ≪≫ pointTranslation G y z = pointTranslation G x z := by
   138	  simp [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_assoc]
   139	
   140	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   141	theorem comp_pointTranslation_hom (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   142	    x ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).hom = y := by
   143	  rw [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, ← Category.assoc,
   144	    comp_mulRight_inv, comp_mulRight_hom, toUnit_unit,
   145	    Category.id_comp, Category.id_comp, mul_inv_cancel, _root_.one_mul]
   146	
   147	/- The inverse translation carries `y` back to `x`; keeping this as a named
   148	   simp lemma avoids repeating the symmetry rewrite at geometric use sites. -/
   149	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   150	theorem comp_pointTranslation_inv (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   151	    y ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).inv = x := by
   152	  exact comp_pointTranslation_hom (G := G) y x

   183	variable {W Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced W] [JacobsonSpace W] [Z.IsSeparated]
   184	
   185	/-- Two morphisms from a reduced Jacobson scheme into a separated scheme are
   186	equal when their residue-field probes agree at every closed point. -/
   187	theorem morphism_eq_of_eqAt_closedPoints
   188	    {g₁ g₂ : W ⟶ Z}
   189	    (h : ∀ x ∈ closedPoints W,
   190	      W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₁ = W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₂) :
   191	    g₁ = g₂ := by
   192	  let F : closedPoints W → Scheme.{u} := fun x => Spec (W.residueField x.1)
   193	  let probe : (∐ F) ⟶ W := Sigma.desc fun x => W.fromSpecResidueField x.1
   194	  haveI : IsDominant probe := by
   195	    refine ⟨(dense_iff_closure_eq.mpr (closure_closedPoints (X := W))).mono ?_⟩
   196	    intro x hx
   197	    obtain ⟨pt⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (W.residueField x)) := inferInstance
   198	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt, ?_⟩
   199	    have hcomp : Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩ ≫ probe = W.fromSpecResidueField x :=
   200	      Sigma.ι_desc _ _
   201	    have e1 : probe.base ((Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt) =
   202	        (W.fromSpecResidueField x).base pt := by
   203	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, hcomp]
   204	    rw [e1]
   205	    exact Set.eq_of_mem_singleton
   206	      (Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField x ▸ Set.mem_range_self pt)
   207	  refine ext_of_isDominant probe (Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_)
   208	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, Sigma.ι_desc]
   209	  exact h x.1 x.2

   219	/-! A proper integral scheme over an algebraically closed field has no
   220	nonconstant maps to an affine scheme.  This is the slice-constancy bridge in
   221	Form I of the rigidity lemma. -/
   222	
   223	theorem eq_comp_of_isAffine_of_properIntegral
   224	    [IsAlgClosed kbar]
   225	    {W : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral W] (wk : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar))
   226	    [UniversallyClosed wk] [LocallyOfFiniteType wk]
   227	    {V : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine V] (g : W ⟶ V)
   228	    (a b : Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar) ⟶ W)
   229	    (ha : a ≫ wk = 𝟙 _) (hb : b ≫ wk = 𝟙 _) :
   230	    a ≫ g = b ≫ g := by
   231	  letI : Field Γ(W, ⊤) :=
   232	    (isField_of_universallyClosed (CommRingCat.of kbar) wk).toField
   233	  set F : CommRingCat.of kbar ⟶ Γ(W, ⊤) :=
   234	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of kbar)).inv ≫ wk.appTop with hF
   235	  have hint : F.hom.IsIntegral := by
   236	    apply RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso.2
   237	      (e := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv)
   238	    exact isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed wk
   239	  haveI : IsIso F := (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective F).mpr
   240	    (IsAlgClosed.ringHom_bijective_of_isIntegral F.hom hint)
   241	  haveI : IsIso wk.appTop := by
   242	    have heq : wk.appTop = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of kbar)).hom ≫ F := by
   243	      rw [hF]
   244	      simp
   245	    rw [heq]
   246	    infer_instance
   247	  have haa : wk.appTop ≫ a.appTop = 𝟙 _ := by
   248	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, ha]
   249	    simp
   250	  have hbb : wk.appTop ≫ b.appTop = 𝟙 _ := by
   251	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hb]
   252	    simp
   253	  have hab : a.appTop = b.appTop := by
   254	    rw [← cancel_epi wk.appTop, haa, hbb]
   255	  apply ext_of_isAffine
   256	  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hab]
   257	
   258	/-! Integrality descends along a scheme-theoretic retract.  The section makes
   259	the retraction surjective on points, while the stalk map of the retraction is
   260	injective because it is a factor of an isomorphism. -/
   261	
   262	theorem isIntegral_of_retract {S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral T]
   263	    (r : S ⟶ T) (pr : T ⟶ S) (hrp : r ≫ pr = 𝟙 S) : IsIntegral S := by
   264	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective pr.base := by
   265	    intro x
   266	    refine ⟨r.base x, ?_⟩
   267	    have h := congrArg (fun m => m.base x) hrp
   268	    simpa using h
   269	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace S := by
   270	    rw [irreducibleSpace_def]
   271	    have h := (IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ T).image pr.base
   272	      pr.base.hom.continuous.continuousOn
   273	    rwa [Set.image_univ, hsurj.range_eq] at h
   274	  haveI hstalk : ∀ x : S, _root_.IsReduced (S.presheaf.stalk x) := by
   275	    intro x
   276	    haveI hiso : IsIso ((r ≫ pr).stalkMap x) := by
   277	      rw [Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_congr_hom (r ≫ pr) (𝟙 S) hrp x,
   278	        Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_id]
   279	      exact inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((S.presheaf.stalkCongr _).hom ≫ 𝟙 _))
   280	    rw [Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_comp] at hiso
   281	    have hbij := (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
   282	      (pr.stalkMap (r.base x) ≫ r.stalkMap x)).1 hiso
   283	    have hinj : Function.Injective (pr.stalkMap (r.base x)).hom := by
   284	      intro a b hab
   285	      apply hbij.injective
   286	      rw [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ConcreteCategory.comp_apply]
   287	      exact congrArg (r.stalkMap x) hab
   288	    have hb : pr.base (r.base x) = x := by
   289	      have h := congrArg (fun m => m.base x) hrp
   290	      simpa using h
   291	    have hred : _root_.IsReduced (S.presheaf.stalk (pr.base (r.base x))) :=
   292	      isReduced_of_injective (pr.stalkMap (r.base x)).hom hinj
   293	    rwa [hb] at hred
   294	  haveI : IsReduced S := isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk S
   295	  exact isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced S

   299	section Scheme

   303	variable {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
   304	
   305	/-- The underlying-scheme isomorphism induced by a translation of sections. -/
   306	noncomputable def pointTranslationIso (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) : G.left ≅ G.left :=
   307	  (Over.forget S).mapIso (pointTranslation G x y)
   308	
   309	@[simp]
   310	theorem pointTranslationIso_hom (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) :
   311	    (pointTranslationIso G x y).hom = (pointTranslation G x y).hom.left :=
   312	  rfl
   313	
   314	@[simp]
   315	theorem pointTranslationIso_inv (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) :
   316	    (pointTranslationIso G x y).inv = (pointTranslation G x y).inv.left :=
   317	  rfl
   318	
   319	@[simp]
   320	theorem pointTranslationIso_self (x : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) :
   321	    pointTranslationIso G x x = Iso.refl G.left := by
   322	  apply Iso.ext
   323	  simp [pointTranslationIso]
   324	
   325	@[simp]

   328	  apply Iso.ext
   329	  simp [pointTranslationIso, pointTranslation]
   330	
   331	@[simp]
   332	theorem pointTranslationIso_trans (x y z : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) :
   333	    pointTranslationIso G x y ≪≫ pointTranslationIso G y z =
   334	      pointTranslationIso G x z := by

   336	  simp [pointTranslationIso, pointTranslation, Iso.trans_assoc]
   337

   340	    (pointTranslationIso G x y).hom ≫ G.hom = G.hom :=
   341	  Over.w _
   342	
   343	@[simp]
   344	theorem pointTranslationIso_hom_apply (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) (s : S) :
   345	    (pointTranslationIso G x y).hom (x.left s) = y.left s := by
   346	  rw [pointTranslationIso_hom, ← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, ← Over.comp_left,

   351	section Transport

   353	open AlgebraicGeometry

   355	/-- Smooth-locus membership is invariant under an automorphism over the base. -/
   356	theorem mem_smoothLocus_iff_of_comp_eq {X S : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion e]
   357	    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (he : e ≫ f = f) (z : X) :
   358	    e z ∈ f.smoothLocus ↔ z ∈ f.smoothLocus := by
   359	  conv_lhs => rw [← Scheme.Hom.mem_preimage]
   360	  rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_smoothLocus_eq]
   361	  simp only [he]
   362	
   363	/-- Reducedness of a stalk is invariant under an open immersion. -/
   364	theorem isReduced_stalk_iff_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ Y)
   365	    [IsOpenImmersion e] (z : X) :
   366	    _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk z) ↔ _root_.IsReduced (Y.presheaf.stalk (e z)) := by
   367	  constructor
   368	  · intro h
   369	    exact isReduced_of_injective (asIso (e.stalkMap z)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   370	      (asIso (e.stalkMap z)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.injective
   371	  · intro h
   372	    exact isReduced_of_injective (asIso (e.stalkMap z)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm
   373	      (asIso (e.stalkMap z)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm.injective
   374	
   375	/-- Irreducibility of a subset is invariant under an isomorphism (preimage form). -/
   376	theorem isIrreducible_preimage_iff_of_isIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso e]
   377	    (t : Set Y) : IsIrreducible (e ⁻¹' t) ↔ IsIrreducible t := by
   378	  have hcoe : ⇑(Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso e)) = ⇑e := by
   379	    rw [Scheme.coe_homeoOfIso, asIso_hom]
   380	  constructor
   381	  · intro hi
   382	    have hsurj : Function.Surjective ⇑e := by
   383	      rw [← hcoe]
   384	      exact (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso e)).surjective
   385	    have h2 := hi.image ⇑e e.continuous.continuousOn
   386	    rwa [Set.image_preimage_eq t hsurj] at h2
   387	  · intro ht
   388	    refine ht.preimage ?_ ?_
   389	    · rw [← hcoe]
   390	      exact (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso e)).isOpenEmbedding
   391	    · have hr : Set.range ⇑e = Set.univ := by
   392	        rw [← hcoe]
   393	        exact (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso e)).surjective.range_eq
   394	      rw [hr, Set.inter_univ]
   395	      exact ht.nonempty
   396

   398	theorem pointTranslationIso_mem_smoothLocus_iff {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
   399	    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.hom] (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) (z : G.left) :
   400	    (pointTranslationIso G x y).hom z ∈ G.hom.smoothLocus ↔ z ∈ G.hom.smoothLocus :=
   401	  mem_smoothLocus_iff_of_comp_eq _ G.hom (pointTranslationIso_hom_comp G x y) z
   402	
   403	/-- Translation preserves reducedness of the local ring at a point. -/
   404	theorem isReduced_stalk_pointTranslationIso_iff {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
   405	    (x y : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G) (z : G.left) :
   406	    _root_.IsReduced (G.left.presheaf.stalk z) ↔

   409

   413	    IsIrreducible ((pointTranslationIso G x y).hom ⁻¹' t) ↔ IsIrreducible t :=
   414	  isIrreducible_preimage_iff_of_isIso _ t

   428	The group-object structure is supplied as a typeclass; the predicate records

   430	def IsAbelianVariety (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] : Prop :=
   431	  IsProper G.hom ∧ GeometricallyIntegral G.hom

   434	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] (hG : IsAbelianVariety G) :
   435	    IsCommMonObj G := by
   436	  letI : IsProper G.hom := hG.1
   437	  letI : GeometricallyIntegral G.hom := hG.2
   438	  exact AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral G
   439	
   440	end AbelianVariety

    97	/-- The `n`-torsion of the unit additive circle is `ZMod n`. -/
    98	def unitAddCircle_torsion_equiv_zmod {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    99	    {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0} ≃ ZMod n := by
   100	  letI : NeZero n := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt hn⟩
   101	  have hmem (j : ZMod n) : n • ZMod.toAddCircle j = 0 := by
   102	    apply (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).2
   103	    refine ⟨j.val, j.val_lt, ?_⟩
   104	    rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   105	    norm_num
   106	  let f : ZMod n → {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0} :=
   107	    fun j => ⟨ZMod.toAddCircle j, hmem j⟩
   108	  have hf : Function.Bijective f := by
   109	    constructor
   110	    · intro a b hab
   111	      exact ZMod.toAddCircle_injective n (Subtype.mk.inj hab)
   112	    · intro u
   113	      obtain ⟨m, hm, hu⟩ := (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).1 u.property
   114	      refine ⟨(m : ZMod n), ?_⟩
   115	      apply Subtype.ext
   116	      change ZMod.toAddCircle (m : ZMod n) = u.val
   117	      rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   118	      simpa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hm] using hu
   119	  exact (Equiv.ofBijective f hf).symm

   121	/-- The torsion of a product torus is the corresponding product of `ZMod`s. -/
   122	def productTorus_torsion_equiv_pi_zmod {d : Type*} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
   123	    {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} ≃ (d → ZMod n) := by
   124	  let e := unitAddCircle_torsion_equiv_zmod hn
   125	  let f : (d → ZMod n) → {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} := fun z =>
   126	    ⟨fun i => (e.symm (z i)).val, by
   127	      apply (mem_productTorus_torsion_iff (n := n) (fun i => (e.symm (z i)).val)).2
   128	      intro i
   129	      exact (e.symm (z i)).property⟩
   130	  have hf : Function.Bijective f := by
   131	    constructor
   132	    · intro a b hab
   133	      funext i
   134	      have hi : (e.symm (a i)).val = (e.symm (b i)).val :=
   135	        congrFun (Subtype.mk.inj hab) i
   136	      have heq : e.symm (a i) = e.symm (b i) := Subtype.ext hi
   137	      simpa using congrArg e heq
   138	    · intro x
   139	      have hx : ∀ i, n • x.val i = 0 :=
   140	        (mem_productTorus_torsion_iff (n := n) x.val).1 x.property
   141	      refine ⟨fun i => e ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩, ?_⟩
   142	      apply Subtype.ext
   143	      funext i
   144	      change (e.symm (e ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩)).val = x.val i
   145	      exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.symm_apply_apply ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩)
   146	  exact (Equiv.ofBijective f hf).symm

   256	    funext i
   257	    rw [Pi.smul_apply, AddMonoidHom.piMap_apply]
   258	    apply (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).2
   259	    refine ⟨(z i).val, (z i).val_lt, ?_⟩
   260	    rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   261	    norm_num
   262	  let f : (d → ZMod n) →+ H :=
   263	    (AddMonoidHom.piMap (fun _ : d => ZMod.toAddCircle)).codRestrict H hmem
   264	  have hf : Function.Bijective f := by
   265	    constructor
   266	    · intro a b hab
   267	      funext i
   268	      apply ZMod.toAddCircle_injective n
   269	      have hi := congrFun (congrArg Subtype.val hab) i
   270	      change ZMod.toAddCircle (a i) = ZMod.toAddCircle (b i) at hi
   271	      exact hi
   272	    · intro x
   273	      have hx : ∀ i, n • x.val i = 0 :=
   274	        (mem_productTorus_torsion_iff (n := n) x.val).1 x.property
   275	      have hex (i : d) : ∃ z : ZMod n, ZMod.toAddCircle z = x.val i := by
   276	        obtain ⟨m, hm, hu⟩ := (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).1 (hx i)
   277	        refine ⟨(m : ZMod n), ?_⟩
   278	        rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   279	        simpa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hm] using hu
   280	      choose z hz using hex
   281	      refine ⟨z, ?_⟩
   282	      apply Subtype.ext
   283	      funext i
   284	      change (AddMonoidHom.piMap (fun _ : d => ZMod.toAddCircle)) z i = x.val i
   285	      rw [AddMonoidHom.piMap_apply]
   286	      exact hz i
   287	  exact (AddEquiv.ofBijective f hf).symm
   288	
   289	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion additive subgroup of the unit circle. -/
   290	def unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup (n : ℤ) : AddSubgroup UnitAddCircle where
   291	  carrier := {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0}
   292	  zero_mem' := by simp
   293	  add_mem' := by
   294	    intro a b ha hb
   295	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha hb ⊢
   296	    rw [zsmul_add, ha, hb, add_zero]
   297	  neg_mem' := by
   298	    intro a ha
   299	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha ⊢
   300	    rw [zsmul_neg, ha, neg_zero]
   301	
   302	/- Signed torsion is the natural torsion subgroup at the absolute value. -/
   303	theorem unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup_eq_torsion (n : ℤ) :
   304	    unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup n =
   305	      unitAddCircle_torsionSubgroup n.natAbs := by
   306	  apply AddSubgroup.ext
   307	  intro u
   308	  change n • u = 0 ↔ n.natAbs • u = 0
   309	  exact natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero.symm
   310	
   311	/-- Integer torsion on the unit circle is additively equivalent to `ZMod |n|`. -/
   312	def unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsion_addEquiv_zmod {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   313	    unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup n ≃+ ZMod n.natAbs := by
   314	  have hpos : 0 < n.natAbs := Int.natAbs_pos.mpr hn
   315	  let f : unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup n ≃+
   316	      unitAddCircle_torsionSubgroup n.natAbs :=
   317	    { toFun := fun u => ⟨u.val, (natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero).2 u.property⟩
   318	      invFun := fun u => ⟨u.val, (natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero).1 u.property⟩
   319	      left_inv := by intro u; exact Subtype.ext rfl
   320	      right_inv := by intro u; exact Subtype.ext rfl
   321	      map_add' := by intro a b; rfl }
   322	  exact f.trans (unitAddCircle_torsion_addEquiv_zmod hpos)
   323	
   324	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion additive subgroup of a product torus. -/
   325	def productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup (d : Type*) (n : ℤ) :
   326	    AddSubgroup (ProductTorus d) where
   327	  carrier := {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0}
   328	  zero_mem' := by simp
   329	  add_mem' := by
   330	    intro a b ha hb
   331	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha hb ⊢
   332	    rw [zsmul_add, ha, hb, add_zero]
   333	  neg_mem' := by
   334	    intro a ha
   335	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha ⊢
   336	    rw [zsmul_neg, ha, neg_zero]
   337	
   338	/- The product-torus version of the absolute-value identification. -/
   339	theorem productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup_eq_torsion (d : Type*) (n : ℤ) :
   340	    productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup d n =
   341	      productTorus_torsionSubgroup d n.natAbs := by
   342	  apply AddSubgroup.ext
   343	  intro x
   344	  change n • x = 0 ↔ n.natAbs • x = 0
   345	  exact natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero.symm
   346	
   347	/-- Integer product-torus torsion is additively equivalent to a product of `ZMod`s. -/
   348	def productTorus_zsmul_torsion_addEquiv_pi_zmod {d : Type*} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   349	    productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup d n ≃+ (d → ZMod n.natAbs) := by
   350	  have hpos : 0 < n.natAbs := Int.natAbs_pos.mpr hn
   351	  let f : productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup d n ≃+
   352	      productTorus_torsionSubgroup d n.natAbs :=
   353	    { toFun := fun x => ⟨x.val, (natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero).2 x.property⟩
   354	      invFun := fun x => ⟨x.val, (natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero).1 x.property⟩
   355	      left_inv := by intro x; exact Subtype.ext rfl
   356	      right_inv := by intro x; exact Subtype.ext rfl
   357	      map_add' := by intro a b; rfl }
   358	  exact f.trans (productTorus_torsion_addEquiv_pi_zmod hpos)
   359	
   360	/-! The additive-subgroup carriers inherit the explicit cardinality formulas. -/
   361	
   362	/-- The positive `n`-torsion subgroup of the unit circle has order `n`. -/
   363	theorem unitAddCircle_torsionSubgroup_card {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
   364	    Nat.card (unitAddCircle_torsionSubgroup n) = n := by
   365	  simpa [unitAddCircle_torsionSubgroup] using (unitAddCircle_torsion_card hn)
   366	
   367	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion subgroup of the unit circle has order `|n|`. -/
   368	theorem unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup_card {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   369	    Nat.card (unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup n) = n.natAbs := by
   370	  simpa [unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsionSubgroup] using
   371	    (unitAddCircle_zsmul_torsion_card hn)
   372	
   373	/-- The positive `n`-torsion subgroup of a finite product torus has order
   374	`n ^ |d|`. -/
   375	theorem productTorus_torsionSubgroup_card {d : Type*} [Fintype d] {n : ℕ}
   376	    (hn : 0 < n) :
   377	    Nat.card (productTorus_torsionSubgroup d n) = n ^ Fintype.card d := by
   378	  simpa [productTorus_torsionSubgroup] using (productTorus_torsion_card (d := d) hn)
   379	
   380	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion subgroup of a finite product torus has order
   381	`|n| ^ |d|`. -/
   382	theorem productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup_card {d : Type*} [Fintype d] {n : ℤ}
   383	    (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   384	    Nat.card (productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup d n) = n.natAbs ^ Fintype.card d := by
   385	  simpa [productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup] using
   386	    (productTorus_zsmul_torsion_card (d := d) hn)
   387	
   388	/-! The set-level finiteness statements also apply directly to subgroup
   389	carriers, which is useful when switching between set and additive-subgroup
   390	interfaces. -/
   391	
   392	/-- The positive torsion subgroup has a finite carrier on a finite product torus. -/
   393	theorem productTorus_torsionSubgroup_carrier_finite
   394	    {d : Type*} [Finite d] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
   395	    ((productTorus_torsionSubgroup d n : AddSubgroup (ProductTorus d)) :
   396	      Set (ProductTorus d)).Finite := by
   397	  simpa [productTorus_torsionSubgroup] using
   398	    (productTorus_torsion_finite (d := d) hn)
   399	
   400	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion subgroup has a finite carrier on a finite
   401	product torus. -/
   402	theorem productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup_carrier_finite
   403	    {d : Type*} [Finite d] {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   404	    ((productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup d n : AddSubgroup (ProductTorus d)) :
   405	      Set (ProductTorus d)).Finite := by
   406	  simpa [productTorus_zsmul_torsionSubgroup] using
   407	    (productTorus_zsmul_torsion_finite (d := d) hn)
   408	
   409	end
   410	
   411	end Mumford

1	/-

     5	-/
     6	
     7	import MumfordLib.Lattice
     8	import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Basic
     9	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Complex.Module
    10	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Pi
    11	import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic
    12	import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Prod
    13	import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Group.Quotient
    14	import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.FiniteDimension
    15	import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.Complex
    16	
    17	/-!
    18	# The complex vector-space model
    19	
    20	The analytic uniformization uses a complex vector space of dimension `g`,
    21	while the underlying real torus has `2 * g` circle factors.  This file makes
    22	that change of coordinates explicit and transports the period-lattice model
    23	through it.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	namespace Mumford
    27	namespace Uniformization
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- The complex vector group of dimension `g`. -/
    32	abbrev GenusComplexVector (g : ℕ) := Fin g → ℂ
    33	
    34	/-- Split a real pair into its two real coordinates. -/
    35	def realPairToFinTwoLinearEquiv : (ℝ × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 2 → ℝ) :=
    36	  (LinearEquiv.finTwoArrow ℝ ℝ).symm
    37	
    38	/-- Uncurry a two-level real coordinate family. -/
    39	def uncurryGenusLinearEquiv (g : ℕ) :
    40	    (Fin g → Fin 2 → ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Fin g × Fin 2 → ℝ) :=
    41	  { toEquiv := (Equiv.curry (Fin g) (Fin 2) ℝ).symm
    42	    map_add' := by
    43	      intro f h
    44	      rfl
    45	    map_smul' := by
    46	      intro r f
    47	      rfl }
    48	
    49	/-- Reindex a pair of finite coordinates as a single `Fin (2 * g)` index. -/
    50	def genusComplexIndexEquiv (g : ℕ) : Fin g × Fin 2 ≃ Fin (2 * g) :=
    51	  (finProdFinEquiv (m := g) (n := 2)).trans
    52	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin (Nat.mul_comm g 2)))
    53	
    54	/-- Reindex real coordinates along `genusComplexIndexEquiv`. -/
    55	def reindexGenusRealLinearEquiv (g : ℕ) :
    56	    (Fin g × Fin 2 → ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] GenusRealVector g :=
    57	  { toEquiv :=
    58	      Equiv.piCongrLeft (fun _ : Fin (2 * g) => ℝ) (genusComplexIndexEquiv g)
    59	    map_add' := by
    60	      intro f h
    61	      funext i
    62	      dsimp [Equiv.piCongrLeft, Equiv.piCongrLeft']
    63	      simp
    64	    map_smul' := by
    65	      intro r f
    66	      funext i
    67	      dsimp [Equiv.piCongrLeft, Equiv.piCongrLeft']
    68	      simp }
    69	
    70	/-- The canonical additive equivalence from complex `g`-coordinates to real
    71	`2g`-coordinates. -/
    72	def genusComplexVectorRealification (g : ℕ) :
    73	    GenusComplexVector g ≃ₗ[ℝ] GenusRealVector g :=
    74	  (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun _ => Complex.equivRealProdLm)).trans
    75	    ((LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun _ => realPairToFinTwoLinearEquiv)).trans
    76	      ((uncurryGenusLinearEquiv g).trans (reindexGenusRealLinearEquiv g)))
    77	
    78	/- The realification is continuous for the standard finite-dimensional
    79	   topologies. -/
    80	theorem genusComplexVectorRealification_continuous (g : ℕ) :
    81	    Continuous (genusComplexVectorRealification g) :=
    82	  (genusComplexVectorRealification g).toLinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional
    83	
    84	/-- The complex-to-real coordinate change evaluated on a paired index. -/
    85	@[simp]
    86	theorem genusComplexVectorRealification_at_index (g : ℕ)
    87	    (z : GenusComplexVector g) (i : Fin g) (j : Fin 2) :
    88	    genusComplexVectorRealification g z (genusComplexIndexEquiv g (i, j)) =
    89	      (realPairToFinTwoLinearEquiv (Complex.equivRealProdLm (z i))) j := by
    90	  have hrr (f : Fin g × Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    91	      reindexGenusRealLinearEquiv g f (genusComplexIndexEquiv g (i, j)) = f (i, j) := by
    92	    change
    93	      (Equiv.piCongrLeft (fun _ : Fin (2 * g) => ℝ)
    94	        (genusComplexIndexEquiv g)) f (genusComplexIndexEquiv g (i, j)) = f (i, j)
    95	    exact Equiv.piCongrLeft_apply_apply (fun _ : Fin (2 * g) => ℝ)
    96	      (genusComplexIndexEquiv g) f (i, j)
    97	  change reindexGenusRealLinearEquiv g
    98	      ((uncurryGenusLinearEquiv g)
    99	        ((LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun _ => realPairToFinTwoLinearEquiv))
   100	          ((LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun _ => Complex.equivRealProdLm)) z)))
   101	      (genusComplexIndexEquiv g (i, j)) = _
   102	  rw [hrr]
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- The period lattice in complex coordinates, obtained by pulling back the
   106	standard integer lattice along realification. -/
   107	def complexPeriodLattice (g : ℕ) : AddSubgroup (GenusComplexVector g) :=
   108	  AddSubgroup.comap (genusComplexVectorRealification g).toAddMonoidHom
   109	    (integerPeriodLattice g)
   110	
   111	/-- The coordinatewise exponential after changing complex coordinates to real
   112	coordinates. -/
   113	def complexGenusTorusExponential (g : ℕ) :
   114	    GenusComplexVector g →+ GenusTorus g :=
   115	  (genusTorusExponential g).comp
   116	    (genusComplexVectorRealification g).toAddMonoidHom
   117	
   118	/- The realified complex-coordinate exponential is continuous. -/
   119	theorem complexGenusTorusExponential_continuous (g : ℕ) :
   120	    Continuous (complexGenusTorusExponential g) := by
   121	  exact (genusTorusExponential_continuous g).comp
   122	    (genusComplexVectorRealification_continuous g)
   123	
   124	/-- The realified exponential is surjective. -/
   125	theorem complexGenusTorusExponential_surjective (g : ℕ) :
   126	    Function.Surjective (complexGenusTorusExponential g) := by
   127	  intro y
   128	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := genusTorusExponential_surjective g y
   129	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := (genusComplexVectorRealification g).surjective v
   130	  refine ⟨z, ?_⟩
   131	  change genusTorusExponential g (genusComplexVectorRealification g z) = y
   132	  rw [hz, hv]
   133	
   134	/-- The pulled-back integer lattice is exactly the kernel of the realified
   135	exponential. -/
   136	theorem complexGenusTorusExponential_ker (g : ℕ) :
   137	    (complexGenusTorusExponential g).ker = complexPeriodLattice g := by
   138	  ext z
   139	  change genusTorusExponential g (genusComplexVectorRealification g z) = 0 ↔
   140	    genusComplexVectorRealification g z ∈ integerPeriodLattice g
   141	  rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker, genusTorusExponential_ker]
   142	
   143	/-- A complex-coordinate period-lattice quotient certificate. -/
   144	def standardComplexGenusPeriodLatticeQuotient (g : ℕ) :
   145	    PeriodLatticeQuotient (GenusComplexVector g) (GenusTorus g) where
   146	  periodLattice := complexPeriodLattice g
   147	  exponential := complexGenusTorusExponential g
   148	  exponential_surjective := complexGenusTorusExponential_surjective g
   149	  kernel_exponential := complexGenusTorusExponential_ker g
   150	
   151	/-- The complex-coordinate quotient is equivalent to the standard genus torus. -/
   152	def complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv (g : ℕ) :
   153	    GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g ≃+ GenusTorus g :=
   154	  (standardComplexGenusPeriodLatticeQuotient g).quotientAddEquiv
   155	
   156	@[simp]
   157	theorem complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv_mk (g : ℕ) (z : GenusComplexVector g) :
   158	    complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g
   159	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z) =
   160	      complexGenusTorusExponential g z := by
   161	  exact PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk
   162	    (standardComplexGenusPeriodLatticeQuotient g) z
   163	
   164	/- Two complex representatives define the same quotient point exactly when
   165	   their difference is a complex period. -/
   166	theorem complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff (g : ℕ)
   167	    (z w : GenusComplexVector g) :
   168	    complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g
   169	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z) =
   170	      complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g
   171	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) w) ↔
   172	      z - w ∈ complexPeriodLattice g := by
   173	  exact PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff
   174	    (standardComplexGenusPeriodLatticeQuotient g) z w
   175	
   176	/- The realification carries the complex period quotient to the standard real
   177	   period quotient. -/
   178	def complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom (g : ℕ) :
   179	    (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) →+
   180	      (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) :=
   181	  QuotientAddGroup.map (complexPeriodLattice g) (integerPeriodLattice g)
   182	    (genusComplexVectorRealification g).toAddMonoidHom (by
   183	      intro z hz
   184	      exact AddSubgroup.mem_comap.mp hz)
   185	
   186	def realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom (g : ℕ) :
   187	    (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) →+
   188	      (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) :=
   189	  QuotientAddGroup.map (integerPeriodLattice g) (complexPeriodLattice g)
   190	    (genusComplexVectorRealification g).symm.toAddMonoidHom (by
   191	      intro v hv
   192	      change genusComplexVectorRealification g
   193	          ((genusComplexVectorRealification g).symm v) ∈ integerPeriodLattice g
   194	      simpa only [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using hv)
   195	
   196	/- The quotient map induced by realification is continuous. -/
   197	theorem complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom_continuous (g : ℕ) :
   198	    Continuous (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom g) := by
   199	  rw [(QuotientAddGroup.isQuotientMap_mk
   200	    (complexPeriodLattice g)).continuous_iff]
   201	  change Continuous (fun z : GenusComplexVector g =>
   202	    QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g)
   203	      (genusComplexVectorRealification g z))
   204	  exact QuotientAddGroup.continuous_mk.comp
   205	    (genusComplexVectorRealification_continuous g)
   206	
   207	/- The inverse quotient map induced by the inverse realification is continuous. -/
   208	theorem realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom_continuous (g : ℕ) :
   209	    Continuous (realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom g) := by
   210	  rw [(QuotientAddGroup.isQuotientMap_mk
   211	    (integerPeriodLattice g)).continuous_iff]
   212	  change Continuous (fun v : GenusRealVector g =>
   213	    QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g)
   214	      ((genusComplexVectorRealification g).symm v))
   215	  exact QuotientAddGroup.continuous_mk.comp
   216	    ((genusComplexVectorRealification g).symm.toLinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional)
   217	
   218	theorem realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom_comp (g : ℕ) :
   219	    (realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom g).comp
   220	        (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom g) = AddMonoidHom.id _ := by
   221	  apply AddMonoidHom.ext
   222	  intro q
   223	  refine QuotientAddGroup.induction_on q ?_
   224	  intro z
   225	  simp [complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom,
   226	    realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom]
   227	
   228	theorem complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom_comp (g : ℕ) :
   229	    (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom g).comp
   230	        (realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom g) = AddMonoidHom.id _ := by
   231	  apply AddMonoidHom.ext
   232	  intro q
   233	  refine QuotientAddGroup.induction_on q ?_
   234	  intro v
   235	  simp [complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom,
   236	    realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom]
   237	
   238	/-- The additive equivalence between the complex and real period quotients. -/
   239	def complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv (g : ℕ) :
   240	    (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) ≃+
   241	      (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) :=
   242	  AddMonoidHom.toAddEquiv (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom g)
   243	    (realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom g)
   244	    (realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom_comp g)
   245	    (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom_comp g)
   246	
   247	/-- The complex and real period quotients are homeomorphic as additive groups. -/
   248	noncomputable def complexQuotientToRealQuotientHomeomorph (g : ℕ) :
   249	    (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) ≃ₜ
   250	      (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) :=
   251	  { complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g with
   252	    continuous_toFun := complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom_continuous g
   253	    continuous_invFun := realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom_continuous g }
   254	
   255	@[simp]
   256	theorem complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv_mk (g : ℕ)
   257	    (z : GenusComplexVector g) :
   258	    complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g
   259	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z) =
   260	      QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g)
   261	        (genusComplexVectorRealification g z) := by
   262	  change complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom g
   263	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z) = _
   264	  simp [complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddHom]
   265	
   266	@[simp]
   267	theorem realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddEquiv_mk (g : ℕ)
   268	    (v : GenusRealVector g) :
   269	    (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g).symm
   270	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   271	      QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g)
   272	        ((genusComplexVectorRealification g).symm v) := by
   273	  change realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom g
   274	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) = _
   275	  simp [realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddHom]
   276	
   277	/- The converse representative criterion is useful when a real period
   278	   calculation is transported back to complex coordinates. -/
   279	theorem realQuotientToComplexQuotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff (g : ℕ)
   280	    (v w : GenusRealVector g) :
   281	    (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g).symm
   282	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   283	      (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g).symm
   284	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) w) ↔
   285	      v - w ∈ integerPeriodLattice g := by
   286	  constructor
   287	  · intro h
   288	    have h' : QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v =
   289	        QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) w := by
   290	      simpa only [AddEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using
   291	        congrArg (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g) h
   292	    have hreal :
   293	        genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   294	            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   295	          genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   296	            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) w) :=
   297	      congrArg (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g) h'
   298	    exact (PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff
   299	      (standardGenusTorusPeriodLatticeQuotient g) v w).mp hreal
   300	  · intro h
   301	    have hreal :
   302	        genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   303	            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   304	          genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   305	            (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) w) :=
   306	      (PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff
   307	        (standardGenusTorusPeriodLatticeQuotient g) v w).mpr h
   308	    have h' : QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v =
   309	        QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) w :=
   310	      (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).injective hreal
   311	    exact congrArg (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g).symm h'
   312	
   313	/- The quotient equivalence intertwines the two exponential models. -/
   314	theorem complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv_trans_genusRealVectorQuotient
   315	    (g : ℕ) :
   316	    (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g).trans
   317	        (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g) =
   318	      complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g := by
   319	  apply AddEquiv.ext
   320	  intro q
   321	  refine QuotientAddGroup.induction_on q ?_
   322	  intro z
   323	  change genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   324	      (complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv g
   325	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z)) =
   326	    complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g
   327	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (complexPeriodLattice g) z)
   328	  rw [complexQuotientToRealQuotientAddEquiv_mk,
   329	    genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv_mk,
   330	    complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv_mk]
   331	  rfl
   332	
   333	/-- The complex-coordinate quotient has the expected signed-integer torsion
   334	classification. -/
   335	def complexGenusQuotient_zsmulTorsion_addEquiv {g : ℕ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   336	    zsmulTorsionSubgroup
   337	        (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) n ≃+
   338	      (Fin (2 * g) → ZMod n.natAbs) :=
   339	  (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv (complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g) n).trans
   340	    (productTorus_zsmul_torsion_addEquiv_pi_zmod hn)
   341	
   342	/-- The complex-coordinate quotient has torsion order `|n| ^ (2 * g)`. -/
   343	theorem complexGenusQuotient_zsmulTorsion_card {g : ℕ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   344	    Nat.card
   345	        (zsmulTorsionSubgroup
   346	          (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) n) =
   347	      n.natAbs ^ (2 * g) := by
   348	  calc
   349	    Nat.card
   350	        (zsmulTorsionSubgroup
   351	          (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ complexPeriodLattice g) n) =
   352	        Nat.card (zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusTorus g) n) :=
   353	      zsmulTorsion_card_eq_of_addEquiv (complexGenusQuotientAddEquiv g) n
   354	    _ = n.natAbs ^ (2 * g) := genusTorus_zsmulTorsion_card g hn
   355

     9	/-!
    10	# Period-lattice quotients
    11	
    12	This file packages the additive quotient data supplied by analytic uniformization
    13	and constructs the standard real period-lattice model of the genus torus.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	namespace Mumford
    17	namespace Uniformization
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	/-- An additive uniformization certificate with a specified period lattice.
    22	
    23	For an analytic exponential map, `kernel_exponential` identifies the periods
    24	with the kernel. Surjectivity then identifies the lattice quotient with the
    25	target additive group.
    26	-/
    27	structure PeriodLatticeQuotient (V X : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup X] where
    28	  periodLattice : AddSubgroup V
    29	  exponential : V →+ X
    30	  exponential_surjective : Function.Surjective exponential
    31	  kernel_exponential : exponential.ker = periodLattice
    32	
    33	namespace PeriodLatticeQuotient
    34	
    35	/-- The first isomorphism theorem for a period-lattice quotient certificate. -/
    36	def quotientAddEquiv {V X : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup X]
    37	    (u : PeriodLatticeQuotient V X) : V ⧸ u.periodLattice ≃+ X :=
    38	  (QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq u.kernel_exponential.symm).trans
    39	    (QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective
    40	      u.exponential u.exponential_surjective)
    41	
    42	/-- The quotient equivalence agrees with the exponential map on representatives. -/
    43	@[simp]
    44	theorem quotientAddEquiv_mk {V X : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup X]
    45	    (u : PeriodLatticeQuotient V X) (v : V) :
    46	    u.quotientAddEquiv (QuotientAddGroup.mk' u.periodLattice v) = u.exponential v := by
    47	  simp only [quotientAddEquiv, AddEquiv.trans_apply, QuotientAddGroup.mk'_apply,
    48	    QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq_mk]
    49	  change QuotientAddGroup.kerLift u.exponential (v : V ⧸ u.exponential.ker) =
    50	    u.exponential v
    51	  rw [QuotientAddGroup.kerLift_mk]
    52	
    53	/- Two representatives define the same quotient point exactly when their
    54	   difference is a period. -/
    55	theorem quotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff {V X : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup X]
    56	    (u : PeriodLatticeQuotient V X) (v w : V) :
    57	    u.quotientAddEquiv (QuotientAddGroup.mk' u.periodLattice v) =
    58	        u.quotientAddEquiv (QuotientAddGroup.mk' u.periodLattice w) ↔
    59	      v - w ∈ u.periodLattice := by
    60	  rw [quotientAddEquiv_mk, quotientAddEquiv_mk]
    61	  constructor
    62	  · intro h
    63	    have hz : u.exponential (v - w) = 0 := by
    64	      rw [map_sub, h, sub_self]
    65	    rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker, u.kernel_exponential] at hz
    66	    exact hz
    67	  · intro h
    68	    have hz : u.exponential (v - w) = 0 := by
    69	      rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker, u.kernel_exponential]
    70	      exact h
    71	    have heq : u.exponential v - u.exponential w = 0 := by
    72	      simpa only [map_sub] using hz
    73	    exact sub_eq_zero.mp heq
    74	
    75	end PeriodLatticeQuotient
    76	
    77	/-- The real vector group underlying a complex torus of dimension `g`. -/
    78	abbrev GenusRealVector (g : ℕ) := Fin (2 * g) → ℝ
    79	
    80	/-- The coordinatewise integer lattice in the real vector group of dimension `2 * g`. -/
    81	def integerPeriodLattice (g : ℕ) : AddSubgroup (GenusRealVector g) :=
    82	  AddSubgroup.pi Set.univ (fun _ => AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ))
    83	
    84	/-- The additive exponential map from the real line to the unit additive circle. -/
    85	def unitAddCircleExponential : ℝ →+ UnitAddCircle :=
    86	  QuotientAddGroup.mk' (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ))
    87	
    88	/-- The coordinatewise exponential from the real vector group to the genus torus. -/
    89	def genusTorusExponential (g : ℕ) : GenusRealVector g →+ GenusTorus g :=
    90	  AddMonoidHom.piMap (fun _ => unitAddCircleExponential)
    91	
    92	/-- The coordinatewise exponential is continuous for the product topologies. -/
    93	theorem genusTorusExponential_continuous (g : ℕ) :
    94	    Continuous (genusTorusExponential g) := by
    95	  apply continuous_pi
    96	  intro i
    97	  change Continuous (fun x : Fin (2 * g) → ℝ =>
    98	    QuotientAddGroup.mk' (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ)) (x i))
    99	  exact (AddCircle.continuous_mk' (1 : ℝ)).comp (continuous_apply i)
   100	
   101	/-- The standard genus torus is connected, including the zero-dimensional case. -/
   102	theorem genusTorus_isConnected (g : ℕ) :
   103	    IsConnected (Set.univ : Set (GenusTorus g)) := by
   104	  change IsConnected (Set.univ : Set (Fin (2 * g) → UnitAddCircle))
   105	  have hpi : IsConnected ((Set.univ : Set (Fin (2 * g))).pi
   106	      (fun _ : Fin (2 * g) => (Set.univ : Set UnitAddCircle))) := by
   107	    rw [isConnected_univ_pi]
   108	    intro i
   109	    exact isConnected_univ
   110	  simpa only [Set.pi_univ] using hpi
   111	
   112	/-- The standard genus torus is path connected. -/
   113	theorem genusTorus_isPathConnected (g : ℕ) : PathConnectedSpace (GenusTorus g) := by
   114	  letI : Nonempty (GenusTorus g) := ⟨0⟩
   115	  exact
   116	    { nonempty := inferInstance
   117	      joined := by
   118	        intro x y
   119	        exact ⟨Path.pi (fun i => PathConnectedSpace.somePath (x i) (y i))⟩ }
   120	
   121	/-- The standard exponential is an open quotient map onto the genus torus. -/
   122	theorem genusTorusExponential_isOpenQuotientMap (g : ℕ) :
   123	    IsOpenQuotientMap (genusTorusExponential g) := by
   124	  change IsOpenQuotientMap (Pi.map (fun _ : Fin (2 * g) =>
   125	    (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ)) :
   126	      ℝ → UnitAddCircle)))
   127	  exact IsOpenQuotientMap.piMap (fun _ => QuotientAddGroup.isOpenQuotientMap_mk)
   128	
   129	/-- The coordinatewise exponential to the genus torus is surjective. -/
   130	theorem genusTorusExponential_surjective (g : ℕ) :
   131	    Function.Surjective (genusTorusExponential g) := by
   132	  exact Function.Surjective.piMap
   133	    (fun _ => QuotientAddGroup.mk'_surjective (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ)))
   134	
   135	/-- The kernel of the coordinatewise exponential is exactly the integer period lattice. -/
   136	theorem genusTorusExponential_ker (g : ℕ) :
   137	    (genusTorusExponential g).ker = integerPeriodLattice g := by
   138	  ext x
   139	  rw [AddMonoidHom.mem_ker]
   140	  simp only [integerPeriodLattice, AddSubgroup.mem_pi, Set.mem_univ, forall_const]
   141	  constructor
   142	  · intro hx i
   143	    have hxi := congrFun hx i
   144	    change unitAddCircleExponential (x i) = 0 at hxi
   145	    rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker] at hxi
   146	    change x i ∈
   147	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ))).ker at hxi
   148	    simpa only [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk'] using hxi
   149	  · intro hx
   150	    funext i
   151	    rw [Pi.zero_apply]
   152	    change unitAddCircleExponential (x i) = 0
   153	    rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker]
   154	    change x i ∈
   155	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ))).ker
   156	    simpa only [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk'] using hx i
   157	
   158	/-- The standard real period-lattice certificate for the genus torus. -/
   159	def standardGenusTorusPeriodLatticeQuotient (g : ℕ) :
   160	    PeriodLatticeQuotient (GenusRealVector g) (GenusTorus g) where
   161	  periodLattice := integerPeriodLattice g
   162	  exponential := genusTorusExponential g
   163	  exponential_surjective := genusTorusExponential_surjective g
   164	  kernel_exponential := genusTorusExponential_ker g
   165	
   166	/-- The standard additive equivalence between the real lattice quotient and the genus torus. -/
   167	def genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv (g : ℕ) :
   168	    GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g ≃+ GenusTorus g :=
   169	  (standardGenusTorusPeriodLatticeQuotient g).quotientAddEquiv
   170	
   171	/-- The standard quotient equivalence evaluates on a representative by the
   172	coordinatewise additive exponential. -/
   173	@[simp]
   174	theorem genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv_mk (g : ℕ) (v : GenusRealVector g) :
   175	    genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g
   176	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   177	      genusTorusExponential g v := by
   178	  exact PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk
   179	    (standardGenusTorusPeriodLatticeQuotient g) v
   180	
   181	/-- Integer torsion of the standard real lattice quotient is a product of
   182	cyclic groups indexed by the `2 * g` coordinates. -/
   183	def genusRealVectorQuotient_zsmulTorsion_addEquiv {g : ℕ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   184	    zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) n ≃+
   185	      (Fin (2 * g) → ZMod n.natAbs) := by
   186	  exact (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g) n).trans
   187	    (productTorus_zsmul_torsion_addEquiv_pi_zmod hn)
   188	
   189	/-- The standard real lattice quotient has the expected finite torsion order. -/
   190	theorem genusRealVectorQuotient_zsmulTorsion_card {g : ℕ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   191	    Nat.card (zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) n) =
   192	      n.natAbs ^ (2 * g) := by
   193	  calc
   194	    Nat.card (zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) n) =
   195	        Nat.card (zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusTorus g) n) :=
   196	      zsmulTorsion_card_eq_of_addEquiv (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g) n
   197	    _ = n.natAbs ^ (2 * g) := genusTorus_zsmulTorsion_card g hn
   198	
   199	/-- Every nonzero integer acts surjectively on the standard real lattice
   200	quotient. -/
   201	theorem genusRealVectorQuotient_exists_division {g : ℕ}
   202	    (x : GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   203	    ∃ y, n • y = x := by
   204	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := genusTorus_exists_division g (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g x) hn
   205	  refine ⟨(genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).symm z, ?_⟩
   206	  apply (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).injective
   207	  simpa only [map_zsmul, AddEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using hz
   208	
   209	/-- The integer torsion of the standard real lattice quotient is finite. -/
   210	theorem genusRealVectorQuotient_zsmulTorsion_finite {g : ℕ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   211	    Finite (zsmulTorsionSubgroup (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) n) := by
   212	  let u : GenusTorusUniformization
   213	      (GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g) g :=
   214	    ⟨genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g⟩
   215	  exact zsmulTorsion_finite_of_uniformization u hn
   216	
   217	/-- The standard real exponential transported to a chosen uniformized group. -/
   218	def exponential_to {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   219	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) : GenusRealVector g →+ X :=
   220	  u.equiv.symm.toAddMonoidHom.comp (genusTorusExponential g)
   221	
   222	/-- The transported exponential to a chosen uniformized group is surjective. -/
   223	theorem exponential_to_surjective {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   224	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) : Function.Surjective (exponential_to u) := by
   225	  intro x
   226	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := genusTorusExponential_surjective g (u.equiv x)
   227	  refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   228	  change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g y) = x
   229	  rw [hy, u.equiv.symm_apply_apply]
   230	
   231	/-- The transported exponential has the same coordinatewise integer kernel. -/
   232	theorem exponential_to_ker {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   233	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) :
   234	    (exponential_to u).ker = integerPeriodLattice g := by
   235	  ext x
   236	  rw [AddMonoidHom.mem_ker]
   237	  constructor
   238	  · intro hx
   239	    change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g x) = 0 at hx
   240	    have hx' : genusTorusExponential g x = 0 := by
   241	      apply u.equiv.symm.injective
   242	      simpa only [map_zero] using hx
   243	    have hx'' : x ∈ (genusTorusExponential g).ker := (AddMonoidHom.mem_ker).mpr hx'
   244	    rw [genusTorusExponential_ker g] at hx''
   245	    exact hx''
   246	  · intro hx
   247	    have hx' : x ∈ (genusTorusExponential g).ker := by
   248	      rw [genusTorusExponential_ker g]
   249	      exact hx
   250	    have hx'' : genusTorusExponential g x = 0 := (AddMonoidHom.mem_ker).mp hx'
   251	    change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g x) = 0
   252	    rw [hx'', map_zero]
   253	
   254	/-- The period-lattice quotient certificate induced by a genus-torus uniformization. -/
   255	def uniformizedPeriodLatticeQuotient {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   256	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) :
   257	    PeriodLatticeQuotient (GenusRealVector g) X where
   258	  periodLattice := integerPeriodLattice g
   259	  exponential := exponential_to u
   260	  exponential_surjective := exponential_to_surjective u
   261	  kernel_exponential := exponential_to_ker u

   263	/-- A genus-torus uniformization identifies the standard real lattice quotient with its group. -/
   264	def uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   265	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) :
   266	    GenusRealVector g ⧸ integerPeriodLattice g ≃+ X :=
   267	  (uniformizedPeriodLatticeQuotient u).quotientAddEquiv
   268	
   269	/-- The transported quotient equivalence evaluates on representatives by the
   270	transported exponential map. -/
   271	@[simp]
   272	theorem uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv_mk {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   273	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) (v : GenusRealVector g) :
   274	    uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv u
   275	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (integerPeriodLattice g) v) =
   276	      exponential_to u v := by
   277	  exact PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk
   278	    (uniformizedPeriodLatticeQuotient u) v
   279	
   280	/-- The quotient model for a chosen uniformization factors through the standard
   281	torus model and the chosen additive equivalence. -/
   282	theorem uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv_eq_trans {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   283	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) :
   284	    uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv u =
   285	      (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).trans u.equiv.symm := by
   286	  apply AddEquiv.ext
   287	  intro q
   288	  obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := QuotientAddGroup.mk'_surjective (integerPeriodLattice g) q
   289	  rfl

   291	/-- Torsion transport through a quotient and then a chosen uniformization
   292	agrees with the direct quotient classification. -/
   293	theorem uniformizedQuotient_zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_eq_direct
   294	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   295	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   296	    (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv (uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv u) n).trans
   297	        (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_uniformization u hn) =
   298	      genusRealVectorQuotient_zsmulTorsion_addEquiv (g := g) hn := by
   299	  rw [uniformizedQuotientAddEquiv_eq_trans u]
   300	  apply AddEquiv.ext
   301	  intro x
   302	  have htransport :
   303	      (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv u.equiv n)
   304	          ((zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv
   305	            ((genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).trans u.equiv.symm) n) x) =
   306	        (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv
   307	          (genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g) n) x := by
   308	    apply Subtype.ext
   309	    simp
   310	  rw [show ((zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv
   311	      ((genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).trans u.equiv.symm) n).trans
   312	      (zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_uniformization u hn)) x =
   313	      (productTorus_zsmul_torsion_addEquiv_pi_zmod hn)
   314	        ((zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv u.equiv n)
   315	          ((zsmulTorsion_addEquiv_of_addEquiv
   316	            ((genusRealVectorQuotientAddEquiv g).trans u.equiv.symm) n) x)) by rfl]
   317	  rw [htransport]
   318	  rfl

     9	/-!
    10	# Group schemes and translations
    11	
    12	This file records the group-object part of Mumford's definition of an abelian
    13	variety.  A section of a group scheme can be moved to any other section by a
    14	canonical right translation.  The construction is completely categorical, so
    15	the same lemmas are available for group objects in any cartesian monoidal
    16	category.
    17	
    18	The final predicate keeps the geometric hypotheses used by the standard
    19	commutativity theorem visible: a proper geometrically integral group scheme
    20	over a field is commutative.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe v u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

    34	section Categorical
    35	
    36	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]
    37	  {G : C} [GrpObj G] {X : C}
    38	
    39	/-- The cartesian identity underlying the rigidity lemma: collapsing the first
    40	variable to a chosen point can be written using either projection. -/
    41	theorem rigidity_snd_lift
    42	    {X Y : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) :
    43	    snd X Y ≫ lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) =
    44	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) := by
    45	  ext1 <;> simp
    46	
    47	/- A categorical factorization form of the rigidity step.  Invariance under
    48	   replacing the first coordinate by `x₀` is equivalent to factoring through
    49	   the second projection. -/
    50	theorem factors_through_snd_iff
    51	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) :
    52	    (∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g) ↔
    53	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f = f := by
    54	  constructor
    55	  · rintro ⟨g, rfl⟩
    56	    rw [← rigidity_snd_lift x₀]
    57	    simp
    58	  · intro h
    59	    refine ⟨lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ f, ?_⟩
    60	    calc
    61	      f = lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f := h.symm
    62	      _ = (snd X Y ≫ lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y)) ≫ f := by
    63	        rw [rigidity_snd_lift x₀]
    64	      _ = snd X Y ≫ (lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ f) :=
    65	        Category.assoc _ _ _
    66	
    67	/-- The factor through the second projection is unique. -/
    68	theorem factor_through_snd_unique
    69	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z)
    70	    {g₁ g₂ : Y ⟶ Z} (h₁ : f = snd X Y ≫ g₁)
    71	    (h₂ : f = snd X Y ≫ g₂) : g₁ = g₂ := by
    72	  have h := congrArg (fun q => lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ q)
    73	    (h₁.symm.trans h₂)
    74	  simpa using h
    75	
    76	/-- The rigidity factorization can be stated with a unique factor. -/
    77	theorem existsUnique_factor_through_snd_iff
    78	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) :
    79	    (∃! g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g) ↔
    80	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f = f := by
    81	  constructor
    82	  · rintro ⟨g, hg, _⟩
    83	    exact (factors_through_snd_iff x₀ f).mp ⟨g, hg⟩
    84	  · intro h
    85	    have hex : ∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g :=
    86	      (factors_through_snd_iff x₀ f).mpr h
    87	    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
    88	    refine ⟨g, hg, ?_⟩
    89	    intro g' hg'
    90	    exact factor_through_snd_unique x₀ f hg' hg
    91	
    92	/-- The group-valued functor of points of a group object. -/
    93	abbrev pointsFunctor (G : C) [GrpObj G] : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat :=
    94	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpObj G
    95	
    96	/-- The functor of points is represented by the underlying group object. -/
    97	def pointsFunctor_representable (G : C) [GrpObj G] :
    98	    (pointsFunctor G ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy G :=
    99	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpObjRepresentableBy G
   100	
   101	/-- The Yoneda functor from group objects to group-valued functors is fully faithful. -/
   102	def pointsYoneda : Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat :=
   103	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrp
   104	
   105	def pointsYoneda_fullyFaithful : (pointsYoneda (C := C)).FullyFaithful :=
   106	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpFullyFaithful
   107	
   108	/-- Composition with a right translation is multiplication in the Hom-group. -/
   109	theorem comp_mulRight_hom (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   110	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).hom = f * (toUnit X ≫ g) := by
   111	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_hom, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   112	    comp_toUnit_assoc, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
   113	
   114	/-- Composition with the inverse right translation is multiplication by the inverse. -/
   115	theorem comp_mulRight_inv (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   116	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).inv = f * (toUnit X ≫ g)⁻¹ := by
   117	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_inv, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   118	    ← Category.assoc, comp_toUnit, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def,
   119	    CategoryTheory.Hom.inv_def, Category.assoc]
   120	
   121	/-- The translation carrying the section `x` to the section `y`. -/
   122	def pointTranslation (G : C) [GrpObj G] (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) : G ≅ G :=
   123	  (GrpObj.mulRight x).symm ≪≫ GrpObj.mulRight y
   124	
   125	@[simp]
   126	theorem pointTranslation_self (x : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   127	    pointTranslation G x x = Iso.refl G := by
   128	  simp [pointTranslation]
   129	
   130	@[simp]
   131	theorem pointTranslation_symm (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   132	    (pointTranslation G x y).symm = pointTranslation G y x := by
   133	  simp [pointTranslation]
   134	
   135	@[simp]
   136	theorem pointTranslation_trans (x y z : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   137	    pointTranslation G x y ≪≫ pointTranslation G y z = pointTranslation G x z := by
   138	  simp [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_assoc]
   139	
   140	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   141	theorem comp_pointTranslation_hom (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   142	    x ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).hom = y := by
   143	  rw [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, ← Category.assoc,
   144	    comp_mulRight_inv, comp_mulRight_hom, toUnit_unit,
   145	    Category.id_comp, Category.id_comp, mul_inv_cancel, _root_.one_mul]
   146	
   147	/- The inverse translation carries `y` back to `x`; keeping this as a named
   148	   simp lemma avoids repeating the symmetry rewrite at geometric use sites. -/
   149	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   150	theorem comp_pointTranslation_inv (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   151	    y ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).inv = x := by
   152	  exact comp_pointTranslation_hom (G := G) y x
   153	
   154	end Categorical

   162	/-- Properness of the first factor makes the second projection a closed map.
   163	
   164	The underlying scheme morphism is the pullback of `X.hom` along `Y.hom`; this
   165	is the geometric input used in the closed-map proof of Mumford's rigidity
   166	lemma. -/
   167	theorem snd_left_isClosedMap
   168	    {X Y : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsProper X.hom] :
   169	    IsClosedMap (snd X Y).left.base := by
   170	  haveI hp : UniversallyClosed X.hom := IsProper.toUniversallyClosed
   171	  haveI : UniversallyClosed (snd X Y).left := by
   172	    rw [Over.snd_left]
   173	    exact universallyClosed_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
   174	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback X.hom Y.hom) hp
   175	  exact Scheme.Hom.isClosedMap _

   183	variable {W Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced W] [JacobsonSpace W] [Z.IsSeparated]
   184	
   185	/-- Two morphisms from a reduced Jacobson scheme into a separated scheme are
   186	equal when their residue-field probes agree at every closed point. -/
   187	theorem morphism_eq_of_eqAt_closedPoints
   188	    {g₁ g₂ : W ⟶ Z}
   189	    (h : ∀ x ∈ closedPoints W,
   190	      W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₁ = W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₂) :
   191	    g₁ = g₂ := by
   192	  let F : closedPoints W → Scheme.{u} := fun x => Spec (W.residueField x.1)
   193	  let probe : (∐ F) ⟶ W := Sigma.desc fun x => W.fromSpecResidueField x.1
   194	  haveI : IsDominant probe := by
   195	    refine ⟨(dense_iff_closure_eq.mpr (closure_closedPoints (X := W))).mono ?_⟩
   196	    intro x hx
   197	    obtain ⟨pt⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (W.residueField x)) := inferInstance
   198	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt, ?_⟩
   199	    have hcomp : Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩ ≫ probe = W.fromSpecResidueField x :=
   200	      Sigma.ι_desc _ _
   201	    have e1 : probe.base ((Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt) =
   202	        (W.fromSpecResidueField x).base pt := by
   203	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, hcomp]
   204	    rw [e1]
   205	    exact Set.eq_of_mem_singleton
   206	      (Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField x ▸ Set.mem_range_self pt)
   207	  refine ext_of_isDominant probe (Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_)
   208	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, Sigma.ι_desc]
   209	  exact h x.1 x.2
   210	
   211	end ClosedPointExtensionality

   217	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar]
   218	
   219	/-! A proper integral scheme over an algebraically closed field has no
   220	nonconstant maps to an affine scheme.  This is the slice-constancy bridge in
   221	Form I of the rigidity lemma. -/
   222	
   223	theorem eq_comp_of_isAffine_of_properIntegral
   224	    [IsAlgClosed kbar]
   225	    {W : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral W] (wk : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar))
   226	    [UniversallyClosed wk] [LocallyOfFiniteType wk]
   227	    {V : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine V] (g : W ⟶ V)
   228	    (a b : Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar) ⟶ W)
   229	    (ha : a ≫ wk = 𝟙 _) (hb : b ≫ wk = 𝟙 _) :
   230	    a ≫ g = b ≫ g := by
   231	  letI : Field Γ(W, ⊤) :=
   232	    (isField_of_universallyClosed (CommRingCat.of kbar) wk).toField
   233	  set F : CommRingCat.of kbar ⟶ Γ(W, ⊤) :=
   234	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of kbar)).inv ≫ wk.appTop with hF
   235	  have hint : F.hom.IsIntegral := by
   236	    apply RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso.2
   237	      (e := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv)
   238	    exact isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed wk
   239	  haveI : IsIso F := (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective F).mpr
   240	    (IsAlgClosed.ringHom_bijective_of_isIntegral F.hom hint)
   241	  haveI : IsIso wk.appTop := by
   242	    have heq : wk.appTop = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of kbar)).hom ≫ F := by
   243	      rw [hF]
   244	      simp
   245	    rw [heq]
   246	    infer_instance
   247	  have haa : wk.appTop ≫ a.appTop = 𝟙 _ := by
   248	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, ha]
   249	    simp
   250	  have hbb : wk.appTop ≫ b.appTop = 𝟙 _ := by
   251	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hb]
   252	    simp
   253	  have hab : a.appTop = b.appTop := by
   254	    rw [← cancel_epi wk.appTop, haa, hbb]
   255	  apply ext_of_isAffine
   256	  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hab]
   257	
   258	/-! Integrality descends along a scheme-theoretic retract.  The section makes
   259	the retraction surjective on points, while the stalk map of the retraction is
   260	injective because it is a factor of an isomorphism. -/
   261	
   262	theorem isIntegral_of_retract {S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral T]
   263	    (r : S ⟶ T) (pr : T ⟶ S) (hrp : r ≫ pr = 𝟙 S) : IsIntegral S := by
   264	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective pr.base := by
   265	    intro x
   266	    refine ⟨r.base x, ?_⟩
   267	    have h := congrArg (fun m => m.base x) hrp
   268	    simpa using h
   269	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace S := by
   270	    rw [irreducibleSpace_def]
   271	    have h := (IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ T).image pr.base
   272	      pr.base.hom.continuous.continuousOn
   273	    rwa [Set.image_univ, hsurj.range_eq] at h
   274	  haveI hstalk : ∀ x : S, _root_.IsReduced (S.presheaf.stalk x) := by
   275	    intro x
   276	    haveI hiso : IsIso ((r ≫ pr).stalkMap x) := by
   277	      rw [Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_congr_hom (r ≫ pr) (𝟙 S) hrp x,
   278	        Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_id]
   279	      exact inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((S.presheaf.stalkCongr _).hom ≫ 𝟙 _))
   280	    rw [Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_comp] at hiso
   281	    have hbij := (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
   282	      (pr.stalkMap (r.base x) ≫ r.stalkMap x)).1 hiso
   283	    have hinj : Function.Injective (pr.stalkMap (r.base x)).hom := by
   284	      intro a b hab
   285	      apply hbij.injective
   286	      rw [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ConcreteCategory.comp_apply]
   287	      exact congrArg (r.stalkMap x) hab
   288	    have hb : pr.base (r.base x) = x := by
   289	      have h := congrArg (fun m => m.base x) hrp
   290	      simpa using h
   291	    have hred : _root_.IsReduced (S.presheaf.stalk (pr.base (r.base x))) :=
   292	      isReduced_of_injective (pr.stalkMap (r.base x)).hom hinj
   293	    rwa [hb] at hred
   294	  haveI : IsReduced S := isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk S
   295	  exact isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced S
   296	
   297	end ProperAffineConstancy

   355	/-- Smooth-locus membership is invariant under an automorphism over the base. -/
   356	theorem mem_smoothLocus_iff_of_comp_eq {X S : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion e]
   357	    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (he : e ≫ f = f) (z : X) :
   358	    e z ∈ f.smoothLocus ↔ z ∈ f.smoothLocus := by
   359	  conv_lhs => rw [← Scheme.Hom.mem_preimage]
   360	  rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_smoothLocus_eq]
   361	  simp only [he]
   362	
   363	/-- Reducedness of a stalk is invariant under an open immersion. -/
   364	theorem isReduced_stalk_iff_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ Y)
   365	    [IsOpenImmersion e] (z : X) :
   366	    _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk z) ↔ _root_.IsReduced (Y.presheaf.stalk (e z)) := by
   367	  constructor
   368	  · intro h
   369	    exact isReduced_of_injective (asIso (e.stalkMap z)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
